title: Iranian American marriage by generation
source: Harris, Kevan, Roxanne Corbeil, and Gilad Wenig. 2024. Iranian Diaspora Dashboard. UCLA Center for Near Eastern Studies.
definition: Share of married Iranian Americans whose spouse is also Iranian (endogamy) versus a spouse of another ancestry (exogamy), from American Community Survey microdata. The project uses “Iranian” to include Persian, Azeri, Kurdish, Armenian, Jewish, Baloch and other Iranian-origin groups.
note: The generational gap is large: first-generation endogamy is about 60% (exogamy ~40%); second-generation endogamy falls to about 20% (exogamy ~80%). The most common spouse category for the second generation is non-Hispanic White. Attitudinal surveys from the 1990s (e.g. Chaichian 1997) found much lower approval of exogamy than today’s behaviour implies.
